summary: This note summarizes the economy of Texas, highlighting its scale if considered as a sovereign country and several indicators of household income, state debt, and population. It compares Texas's 2016 GDP to national economies and notes its household income ranking and debt per taxpayer. It also states that Texas has the second largest population in the United States.
one_line: Overview of the Texas economy, comparing its 2016 GDP to sovereign nations and noting household income, state debt, and population rank.
key_facts: As a sovereign country in 2016, Texas would be the 10th largest economy in the world by GDP.
Texas would rank ahead of South Korea and Canada by GDP if it were a sovereign country in 2016.
Texas's household income in 2010 ranked 25th in the nation.
The state debt of Texas in 2012 was calculated to be $121.7 billion.
The state debt of Texas in 2012 equated to $7,400 per taxpayer.
Texas has the second largest population in the United States.
Texas's population ranks second in the country, behind California.
